title: Unit 1 test: Kinematics
author: p1-1
directions: This practice test has two sections. Section I has 12 multiple-choice questions worth 1 point each; Section II has 2 free-response questions. Any calculator is allowed. Use g = 9.8 m/s^2 and neglect air resistance unless a question says otherwise. Record raw points from the key; they are practice tallies, not AP® scores.

parts.directions: Choose the best answer for each question and mark it on the answer sheet.

items.prompt: Which pair lists a vector quantity followed by a scalar quantity?
items.rationale: Velocity has a direction and is a vector; speed is its magnitude and is a scalar.

distractorNotes.A: Reversed order: speed is the scalar.

items.prompt: A dog runs along a straight path from x = 12 m to x = −20 m and then back to x = −4 m, taking 16 s in all. What is its average velocity?
items.rationale: Average velocity = Δx/Δt = (−4 m − 12 m)/16 s = −1.0 m/s.

distractorNotes.B: Average speed: total distance 48 m divided by 16 s.
distractorNotes.C: Sign error: the dog ends up on the negative side of its start.
distractorNotes.D: Uses the final position instead of the displacement.

items.prompt: A car moving at 15 m/s accelerates uniformly at 2.0 m/s^2 for 5.0 s. How far does it travel during those 5.0 s?

distractorNotes.B: Omits the factor 1/2 in the acceleration term.

items.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up at 19.6 m/s. Taking up as positive and neglecting air resistance, what is its velocity 3.0 s after release?
items.rationale: v = v_0 + at = 19.6 m/s − (9.8 m/s^2)(3.0 s) = −9.8 m/s: the ball passed the top at 2.0 s and is now falling.

distractorNotes.A: Correct size but the wrong sign; the ball is moving down.
distractorNotes.C: Adds the change in velocity instead of subtracting it.
distractorNotes.D: Assumes the ball is at the top; the top is reached at 2.0 s.

items.prompt: The graph shows the position of a toy car moving along a straight track. During which interval is the car's speed greatest?
choices: The speed is the same in every interval
items.rationale: Speed is the magnitude of the slope of a position–time graph: 3 m/s from 0 to 2 s, 0 from 2 to 5 s and 8 m/s from 5 to 6 s.

distractorNotes.A: This interval has a positive slope, but a smaller one in magnitude.
distractorNotes.B: A flat position graph means the car is at rest.
distractorNotes.D: The slopes differ, so the speeds differ.

items.prompt: For the toy car whose position is graphed, what is the average velocity from t = 0 to t = 6 s?
items.rationale: The car goes from x = 0 to x = −2 m in 6 s, so the average velocity is −2 m/6 s ≈ −0.33 m/s.

distractorNotes.A: Average speed: 14 m of total distance divided by 6 s.
distractorNotes.B: Uses only the last segment's displacement, −8 m, over 6 s.
distractorNotes.C: Sign error: the car ends on the negative side of its start.

items.prompt: The graph shows the velocity of an object moving along a line. What is its displacement from t = 0 to t = 6 s?
items.rationale: The area below the axis from 0 to 3 s, −9 m, cancels the area above the axis from 3 to 6 s, +9 m.

distractorNotes.B: Adds the two triangle areas without signs, which gives the distance.
distractorNotes.C: Counts only the area below the axis, doubled.
distractorNotes.D: Treats the region as a rectangle.

items.prompt: For the object whose velocity is graphed, at what time is the object farthest from its starting point on the negative side?
items.rationale: The velocity is negative until t = 3 s, so the object moves in the negative direction until then and turns around when v = 0.

distractorNotes.A: The object is at its starting point at t = 0.
distractorNotes.C: By t = 6 s the positive area has brought the object back to its start.
distractorNotes.D: The object is still moving in the negative direction at 1.5 s.

items.prompt: A swimmer swims upstream at 1.2 m/s relative to the water in a river that flows at 0.50 m/s. What is the swimmer's velocity relative to the riverbank?
items.rationale: Upstream positive: v_SB = v_SW + v_WB = 1.2 m/s + (−0.50 m/s) = +0.70 m/s, upstream.

distractorNotes.B: Correct size but the swimmer outpaces the current, so the motion is upstream.
distractorNotes.C: Adds the speeds as if the current helped.
distractorNotes.D: Combines the velocities as if they were perpendicular.

items.prompt: A survey drone's velocity relative to the air is 7.0 m/s due east, and radar shows that its velocity relative to the ground is 12 m/s due north. What is the velocity of the wind relative to the ground?
items.rationale: v_drone,ground = v_drone,air + v_air,ground, so v_air,ground = (12 m/s north) − (7.0 m/s east): components 7.0 m/s west and 12 m/s north, magnitude √(12^2 + 7.0^2) ≈ 14 m/s, at arctan(7.0/12) ≈ 30° west of north.

distractorNotes.A: Adds the drone's air velocity to its ground velocity instead of subtracting it.
distractorNotes.C: Subtracts the speeds as if the two velocities were parallel.
distractorNotes.D: Adds the magnitudes, 12 m/s + 7.0 m/s, instead of combining perpendicular components.

items.prompt: A ball leaves a horizontal ledge at 6.0 m/s and falls 4.9 m to level ground. Neglecting air resistance, what is its speed just before it lands?

distractorNotes.B: Adds the components as numbers instead of as vectors.

items.prompt: Projectile B is launched from level ground with twice the vertical component of initial velocity of projectile A and the same horizontal component. Projectile A reaches maximum height H and lands a distance R away. What are B's maximum height and range?
items.rationale: Maximum height is v_y^2/(2g), so doubling v_y multiplies it by 4; flight time 2v_y/g doubles, and with the same v_x the range doubles.

distractorNotes.B: Height depends on the square of v_y, not on v_y.
distractorNotes.C: Range scales with flight time, which only doubles.
distractorNotes.D: Doubling the flight time doubles the range.

parts.directions: Show your work and explain your reasoning; points are awarded for correct physics reasoning as well as for answers. Give numerical answers with units. Questions about experiments use supplied data; they do not replace hands-on lab work.

items.prompt: Cart 1 moves along a long, level track. It is at x = 0 at t = 0 and moves in the +x direction at a constant 3.0 m/s until t = 2.0 s. From t = 2.0 s to t = 6.0 s a fan mounted on the cart gives it a constant acceleration of −1.5 m/s^2.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On the grid, sketch the velocity–time graph of cart 1 from t = 0 to t = 6.0 s. Label the velocity at t = 0, 2.0 s and 6.0 s and the time when the velocity is zero.

rubric.criterion: Horizontal segment at +3.0 m/s from t = 0 to t = 2.0 s.
Straight line from (2.0 s, 3.0 m/s) to (6.0 s, −3.0 m/s), slope −1.5 m/s^2.
Line crosses v = 0 at t = 4.0 s (accept 3.9–4.1 s), with labels.

parts.answer: v = 3.0 m/s from 0 to 2.0 s, then a straight line through zero at t = 4.0 s to −3.0 m/s at 6.0 s.
steps: From 2.0 s, v = 3.0 − 1.5(t − 2.0), which is 0 at t = 4.0 s and −3.0 m/s at t = 6.0 s.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: On the grid, sketch the position–time graph of cart 1 for the same interval. Label the position at t = 2.0 s, 4.0 s and 6.0 s.

rubric.criterion: Straight line from the origin to 6.0 m at t = 2.0 s.
Curve bending downward with a horizontal tangent at its maximum, 9.0 m at t = 4.0 s.
Curve returns to 6.0 m at t = 6.0 s, consistent with the velocity graph.

parts.answer: x rises linearly to 6.0 m at 2.0 s, curves to a maximum of 9.0 m at 4.0 s, and returns to 6.0 m at 6.0 s.
steps: x(2.0) = 3.0 × 2.0 = 6.0 m; adding areas under the velocity graph gives +3.0 m from 2.0 to 4.0 s (x = 9.0 m) and −3.0 m from 4.0 to 6.0 s (x = 6.0 m).
Constant velocity gives a straight segment; constant negative acceleration gives a downward-bending curve that is flat where v = 0.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the total distance cart 1 travels and its displacement from t = 0 to t = 6.0 s. Explain how each is represented on your velocity–time graph.

rubric.criterion: Displacement +6.0 m as the signed area (area below the axis subtracted).
Distance 12 m as the total area counted without signs.
Explains the difference: from 4.0 s to 6.0 s the cart moves backward, which subtracts from displacement but adds to distance.

steps: Areas: 0–2.0 s gives +6.0 m, 2.0–4.0 s gives +3.0 m, 4.0–6.0 s gives −3.0 m.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Cart 2 moves at a constant +1.5 m/s on a parallel track and is also at x = 0 at t = 0. Using your position–time graph, explain whether the carts are ever at the same position after t = 0, and if so find the time.

rubric.criterion: Adds x = 1.5t to the position graph or compares positions: cart 1 is ahead at t = 4.0 s (9.0 m against 6.0 m) and behind at t = 6.0 s (6.0 m against 9.0 m), so they meet once in between.
Writes 6.0 + 3.0(t − 2.0) − 0.75(t − 2.0)^2 = 1.5t, or an equivalent equation, or reads the crossing time from an accurately drawn graph with cart 2's line.
Solves t ≈ 5.2 s (accept 5.1–5.3 s), at x ≈ 7.9 m.

parts.answer: Yes, once, at about t = 5.2 s (x ≈ 7.9 m).
steps: t ≈ 5.24 s and x = 1.5 × 5.24 ≈ 7.9 m; before t = 2.0 s cart 1 is always ahead, so this is the only meeting.

items.prompt:
A student wants to find how fast a spring plunger launches a low-friction cart up a long, straight track tilted at a small angle, and the cart's acceleration along the track. Take up the track as positive. A light gate at the launch mark starts a timer when the cart passes it (t = 0), and the cart passes that mark at the same speed in every trial. A second light gate, a distance x farther up the track, stops the timer when the cart first reaches it. The student moves the second gate and records:
| x (m) | 0.40 | 0.70 | 1.00 | 1.30 | 1.60 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| t (s) | 0.281 | 0.524 | 0.788 | 1.121 | 1.538 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe how the student should measure each distance x, and what the student could do to reduce the uncertainty in the times. Identify one source of uncertainty that repeating trials would not remove.

rubric.criterion: Measures x along the track from the beam of the first gate to the beam of the second (where each gate senses the cart), for example with a meter stick laid along the track.
Launches several times at each gate position with the same plunger compression and averages t.
Names a systematic source, such as measuring x to the gate housings instead of the beams or a track tilt that changes when a gate is moved, which shifts every trial the same way.

parts.answer: Measure x along the track between the two light beams with a meter stick; launch several times at each position with the same plunger setting and average t. Repeats cannot remove a systematic error, such as an offset in where the beams are taken to be.
steps: Random scatter in t (small differences between launches) averages out over repeated trials; an offset in x or a change in tilt affects every trial the same way, so repeating does not remove it.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Starting from a kinematic equation for constant acceleration, show that x/t should be a linear function of t. State what the slope and the vertical intercept of a graph of x/t against t represent.

rubric.criterion: Writes x = v_0t + (1/2)at^2 and divides by t to get x/t = v_0 + (a/2)t.
States that the slope is a/2 and the vertical intercept is v_0, the speed at the launch mark.

parts.answer: x = v_0t + (1/2)at^2, so x/t = v_0 + (a/2)t: a graph of x/t against t is a straight line with slope a/2 and vertical intercept v_0.
steps: x/t is the average velocity between the gates; for constant acceleration it changes linearly with t.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: On the grid, plot x/t against t for the data and draw a best-fit line.

rubric.criterion: Computes x/t (1.42, 1.34, 1.27, 1.16, 1.04 m/s) and plots them against t with labeled axes, units and scales.
Draws a single straight best-fit line through the trend of the points (it does not pass through the origin).

parts.answer: x/t (m/s): 1.42, 1.34, 1.27, 1.16, 1.04; the points fall close to a straight line that slopes down.
steps: Divide each x by its t, then plot against t.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Use your line to find the speed of the cart at the launch mark and its acceleration along the track. State the direction of the acceleration.

rubric.criterion: Reads the vertical intercept as v_0 ≈ 1.50 m/s (accept 1.45–1.55 m/s).
Finds the slope from two points on the line, about −0.30 m/s^2 (accept −0.28 to −0.33 m/s^2), and a = 2 × slope ≈ −0.60 m/s^2 (accept −0.56 to −0.66 m/s^2).
Interprets the negative sign: the acceleration points down the track, so the cart slows as it climbs.

parts.answer: v_0 ≈ 1.50 m/s; a ≈ −0.60 m/s^2, that is 0.60 m/s^2 directed down the track.
steps: Using points on the line such as (0.30 s, 1.41 m/s) and (1.50 s, 1.05 m/s), the slope is (1.05 − 1.41)/(1.50 − 0.30) ≈ −0.30 m/s^2.
The line meets t = 0 at about 1.50 m/s, so v_0 ≈ 1.50 m/s; a = 2(−0.30 m/s^2) = −0.60 m/s^2.
